BiblicalUsage: Once in each of two verses, a camp in the wilderness: they removed from Dibon-gad, and encamped in Almon-diblathaim, and they removed from Almon-diblathaim, and pitched in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo. The name is a stopping place on the way to the promised land, and the stopping is all the Bible says of it.
TheologicalSignificance: A camp named twice on the march carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the long road itself, that the way to the promise was measured camp by camp, and none of them was home yet.
